Hi maintainers, this is my first contribution to OpenBMC. Could someone please help to trigger the CI for me? Thanks!
This might not work, since the same class is also used for SMA Temperature Sensor.

I understand that Sensor is a base class used by many sensors. My initial thought was to use a default parameter std::string() to ensure that other sensors remain unaffected if they don't provide a value.

However, I see your point about keeping the base class clean. I will follow your suggestion to restore the Sensor class and register PhysicalContext individually within each sensor class in nvidia-gpu. I will upload a new patch set soon. 

Thanks!
Done

This class is used for Temperature Sensor by for both GPU and SMA device. We need to set Physical Context to correct value based on the device type instead of unconditionally setting it to GPU. I suggest we do this for other sensor type as well.
Done
Is it possible to avoid modifying this class and register PhysicalContext withing each sensor class inside nvidia-gpu?
Done
PDI used LGTM. Needs rebase.
Done

Need more information on the platform that is used for the testing. For nvl32-obmc, please add information on how the BMC image was built, similar to https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/85080/6.
Done
This is not present in the destructor of the other Sensor classes.
Done

I strongly suggest to not do this. The GPU Device class shouldn't be made aware of fully qualified name for GPU PhysicalContext or even of PhysicalContext. I suggest we only pass device type to each Sensor class constructor (using enum already defined in OcpMctpVdm.hpp) and create a helper function to map device type to PhysicalContext and have all Sensor class implementation call that helper function.
Done
